---
title: "Selected images with `lightbox`"
format:
  html:
    code-tools: true
    lightbox: true
filters:
  - path: ../../_filters/show-source.lua
    at: pre-ast
  - panzoom
panzoom:
  hint: false
---

## About {.unnumbered}

lightbox is on for the whole page, and only images marked with the `.panzoom`
class or the `#| panzoom: true` cell option open in panzoom. Every other image
opens in lightbox. The same cases open in lightbox alone on the [lightbox
page](a-lightbox.html), and the same markup without lightbox is on [panzoom on
marked images only](d-panzoom-selective.html). The hint line is off.

```yaml
format:
  html:
    lightbox: true
filters:
  - panzoom
panzoom:
  hint: false
```

## Single image {#c1 expect-open="panzoom"}

A markdown image with `.panzoom` and a description. It opens in panzoom, with
the description below the caption. panzoom has no `desc-position`, so the
image's `desc-position="left"` has no effect.

```markdown {.show-source}
![A markdown image with `.panzoom` with a description and `desc-position="left"`. It opens in panzoom, with the description below the caption, since panzoom has no `desc-position`.](../../images/mv-0.jpg){.panzoom description="Chilmark has _some_ of the best beaches. **credit:** [Chilmark Beach](https://unsplash.com/photos/VBDJGOMCwps)" desc-position="left" fig-alt="Sunset over a sandy beach, with a tall rock stack against the sun"}
```

## Gallery in a layout {#c2 expect-open="glightbox panzoom glightbox"}

Three images in a layout, joined by `group="elsewhere"`. The middle one (Oak
Bluffs) has `.panzoom`, so it opens in panzoom on its own, and panzoom takes it
out of the group. The other two open in lightbox, in a two-image gallery. In
lightbox, a click zooms an image larger than the screen to its full size, and
the wheel doesn't zoom.

```markdown {.show-source}
::: {layout="[[1, 1], [1]]"}
![Aquinnah, joined by `group` with the lighthouse. The two open in lightbox as a two-image gallery.](../../images/mv-1.jpg){group="elsewhere" description="The waves break off Aquinnah." fig-alt="Waves breaking below grassy clay cliffs at Aquinnah"}

![Oak Bluffs, the only one of the three with `.panzoom`. It opens in panzoom on its own.](../../images/mv-3.jpg){.panzoom group="elsewhere" description="Gingerbread cottages." fig-alt="A shingled gingerbread cottage with pink and green trim, behind a garden path"}

![Vineyard lighthouse, in the lightbox gallery with Aquinnah.](../../images/mv-2.jpg){group="elsewhere" description="Edgartown Lighthouse." fig-alt="A white lighthouse against a blue sky"}
:::
```

## Math {#c3 expect-open="panzoom"}

A markdown image with `.panzoom` and math in its caption and description. It
opens in panzoom, with both typeset.

```markdown {.show-source}
![Caption with math $e^{i\pi}+1=0$](../../images/mv-4.jpg){.panzoom description="Description with math $\\int_0^1 x^2\\,dx = 1/3$" fig-alt="A sailboat with a flag-striped sail off a sandy beach"}
```

## Markdown subfigures {#c4 expect-open="panzoom"}

A figure with two markdown subfigures, both with `.panzoom`. Either one opens in
panzoom, in a two-image gallery. The figure's caption links to the heat map in
[case 12](#c12).

```markdown {.show-source}
::: {#fig-md-sub layout-ncol=2}
![Sub A](../../images/mv-1.jpg){#fig-md-a .panzoom fig-alt="Waves breaking below grassy clay cliffs at Aquinnah"}

![Sub B](../../images/mv-2.jpg){#fig-md-b .panzoom fig-alt="A white lighthouse against a blue sky"}

Two markdown subfigures with `.panzoom` and a link to the heat map at the end of the page (see @fig-plain). They open in panzoom as a two-image gallery.
:::
```

## R subfigures {#c5 expect-open="panzoom"}

One R cell with `panzoom: true` and two plots, made subfigures by `fig-subcap`.
Either one opens in panzoom, in a two-image gallery.

```{r}
#| label: fig-r-sub
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Two subfigures from one R cell with `panzoom: true`. They open in panzoom
#|   as a two-image gallery.
#| fig-subcap: ["Pressure", "Cars"]
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Scatter plot of vapor pressure rising steeply with temperature"
#|   - "Scatter plot of stopping distance against speed for 50 cars"
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| panzoom: true

plot(pressure)
plot(cars)
```

## Cell options {#c6 expect-open="panzoom glightbox"}

Two R cells in the lightbox group `r-graph`. The first also has `panzoom: true`,
so it opens in panzoom on its own, without the lightbox description. The second
opens in lightbox, alone in its group.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of ten random points"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   An R cell with `panzoom: true`, with lightbox options too. It opens in
#|   panzoom on its own.
#| panzoom: true
#| lightbox:
#|   group: r-graph
#|   description: Ten random points.

plot(1:10, rnorm(10))
```

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of stopping distance against speed for 50 cars"
#| fig-cap: "An R cell with only lightbox options. It opens in lightbox on its own."
#| lightbox:
#|   group: r-graph
#|   description: Stopping distance against speed.

plot(cars)
```

## Two plots in one cell {#c7 expect-open="panzoom"}

One R cell with `panzoom: true`, two plots, and the lightbox options
`group: cars` and a description for each plot. panzoom drops the lightbox
options, so each plot opens in panzoom on its own, without a description.

```{r}
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Scatterplot matrix of the mtcars data, each variable plotted against every other"
#|   - "Scatter plot of stopping distance against speed for 50 cars"
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap:
#|   - >-
#|     One R cell with `panzoom: true`, two plots, and lightbox options.
#|     panzoom drops the lightbox options, so this plot opens in panzoom on its
#|     own.
#|   - "The second plot of the cell. It also opens in panzoom on its own."
#| lightbox:
#|   group: cars
#|   description:
#|     - The mtcars data, each variable against every other.
#|     - Stopping distance against speed.

plot(mtcars)
plot(cars)
```

## Opt out {#c8 expect-open="nothing"}

An R cell with `lightbox: false` and no `.panzoom`. Neither viewer takes it, so
clicking it does nothing.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "An R cell with `lightbox: false`. Clicking it does nothing."
#| lightbox: false
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Scatterplot matrix of the mtcars data, each variable plotted against every
#|   other

plot(mtcars)
```

## Image in a link {#c9 expect-open="navigation"}

An image with `.panzoom` inside a link. panzoom leaves linked images alone, so
clicking the image follows the link.

```markdown {.show-source}
[![A sailboat off Edgartown, linked to quarto.org.](../../images/mv-4.jpg){.panzoom width=30% fig-alt="A sailboat with a flag-striped sail off a sandy beach, with an unrelated link to open the Quarto website"}](https://quarto.org)
```

## Margin image {#c10 expect-open="panzoom"}

A markdown image with `.panzoom` in the margin. It opens in panzoom, as any
other marked image does.

```markdown {.show-source}
![A gingerbread cottage in Oak Bluffs, placed in the page margin.](../../images/mv-3.jpg){.panzoom .column-margin fig-alt="A shingled gingerbread cottage with pink and green trim, behind a garden path"}
```

## Inline image {#c11 expect-open="panzoom" expect-caption="none"}

An image with `.panzoom` inside a sentence. It opens in panzoom, with no
caption, since an inline image isn't a figure and has none.

```markdown {.show-source}
Some text with an inline image ![A white lighthouse](../../images/mv-2.jpg){.panzoom width=60px} in the middle.
```

## Plain R figure {#c12 expect-open="glightbox"}

A cross-referenced R figure with no options. It opens in lightbox, since it
isn't marked. The caption of [case 4](#c4) links to it.

```{r}
#| label: fig-plain
#| fig-alt: "Heat map of the Maunga Whau volcano's heights, in yellow, orange, and red"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   A cross-referenced R figure with no options. It opens in lightbox, which
#|   the document turns on.

image(volcano)
```
